text: Exhibit A-one. In July two thousand, Enron printed a sixty-four-page Code of Ethics—signed by its executives, pledging total honesty.
Inside these towers in Houston, the stock hit ninety dollars and fifty-six cents, while thirty-eight billion in debt sat hidden off the books.
By December two thousand one, seventy-four billion dollars had vanished. CEO Jeffrey Skilling was sentenced to twenty-four years.
Every signature, every ledger, and every photograph remains on the record.
